text.text: Welcome to Funeral Quest, Ned Digger.  Good luck.
You unlock the front door and enter your beloved Digger & Daughters Funeral Parlor.  Ah, it's great to be alive.
. Snow falling soft and slow. Families feel sentimental and generous.

status.text: Snow (families spend 5% more) Nothing in the paper worth dying for.

text.text:
"Welcome to Deathville, Ned Digger! I'm from the Funeral Director's Guild. Congratulations on Digger & Daughters. It's... a building. It has a door and most of its windows.

I'll walk you through your first day. Two minutes. Or press Skip and learn the hard way, like the last fellow. We buried him Tuesday."

"Cash is for the business. Di-Mart sells caskets wholesale; ask for Elijah, and don't let him touch your hair. Selling from stock pays better than a rush order. Your office has upgrades: paint, a coffee machine, one day a chapel.

That's it! Your first customer is waiting. I'll be watching. Taking notes. Don't mind me."
"My granddaughter is dead and the house is fine. Life isn't fair. I need a wood casket."
asks whether the brochure comes in a leather edition.
"I kept the ticket stub from every movie we saw together. Can those go in with her?"
"I've got a thing at four. Another thing at four-fifteen. Let's move this along."
You figure she can spend between $800 and $2,750.

upgrades.name: Alarm System

You're in one piece, more or less. Injuries from fights would show up here, and on your face.

The Nurse knows who's in intensive care and who won't be leaving it. For
she'll put your card in the right hand.
(-2 karma, a sure and richer customer)

note.text: The hospital smells of bleach and boiled carrots. The Nurse looks up from a crossword about bones, which she is winning.
